packs.title: Historic houses, public learning and park paths
packs.promise: Read reconstructed and historic rooms, collect present-day clues and make from public paths.

q.s: Collect what a farm feature shows and what its interpretation adds.
st: Find the opened farm visitor paths beside the barn area, using the actual museum map and current barriers. Stay within admitted visitor scope rather than entering a work enclosure.

Collect three different currently visible farm-feature records, such as a barn form, a work-area shelter or an interpreted equipment feature. For each, write one actual visible material or arrangement.

Use the linked farm account or a readable onsite interpretation to add a supported work role to each record. Choose another visible feature if its role is not documented; do not identify a tool merely by guessing its use.
Compare two records in one sentence: explain what different work each source describes and what visible evidence you could actually observe. Keep animals, crops and working demonstrations incidental.

q.s: Collect the signs and layouts that let a library visitor find a next step.
st: Reach the opened second-floor public visitor spaces using current directions. Choose three currently visible wayfinding or layout connections among public reading, learning or information areas.
For each, note the actual clue and what a visitor can learn from it. A sign naming a studio or reserved room does not mean you may enter or use its equipment.
Follow one permitted public connection at a comfortable pace. Compare what you expected with what you could actually find, keeping staff-only and occupied booked areas outside your route.
Write a three-item visitor key and one revision after testing the connection. Use your own concise directions rather than copying a sign design, personal document or library map.

q.s: Let a small land path become an outward view and a return.
st: Start at a permitted land-path position near the recorded western visitor trailhead. Use current signs to choose the opened East Shared-Use Trail rather than a paddling route or bike-only alternative.
Walk a comfortable short distance toward the nearby southern bend, noticing one path-shape change and one relationship to the surrounding land view. Yield to other path users.
Turn at that bend or earlier if conditions require it, then return along the same opened route. Keep the actual turnaround distinct from any longer route on the regional map.
Write an outward observation, a return observation and your actual turn. Finish with one detail that changed with your direction; no walking-time target applies.

packs.title: Downtown museums and Cascades afternoons
packs.promise: Connect current galleries, historic rooms and actual public park places across two afternoons.

q.s: Collect a visible form beside its documented material.
st: Enter the opened first-floor exhibition under current visitor directions. Choose three different currently viewable works with readable material or medium information.

For each, record the work’s title or identifier as stated, a documented material or medium, and one visible form relationship. Mark missing information as not stated and choose another supported work rather than guessing its material.
Compare two records: describe how their actual forms use the stated materials differently. Keep your response original rather than copying an artist statement or reproducing the works.
Write the three records and comparison in a permitted note area or from memory after exiting. Use another currently displayed work if a fixed example changes.

q.s: Collect a marker’s visible connections without turning them into a land claim.
st: Find the actual survey marker in its immediate plaza, using opened public paths. Choose a permitted position that leaves circulation and monument approaches clear.

Collect three visible relationships among the marker, surrounding ground pattern and a public path connection. Describe actual placement and edges without copying the inlay design or handling the marker.

Read the linked City account or readable interpretation and paraphrase the supported 1824 survey-starting-point fact. Keep that historical role separate from a modern property boundary or navigation claim.

Write three short relationship records and a plain-language description of how a visitor reaches the marker from the plaza. Add the sourced history fact; do not reproduce a map or supply unmeasured coordinates.

q.s: Notice one crossing from both directions.
st: Reach the opened eastern deck approach on the actual pedestrian path, staying separate from the road below. Choose a comfortable short return and keep shared circulation clear.
Walk to the western deck endpoint or turn earlier if current conditions require it. Notice one canopy or support relationship and one change in the path’s view; no night lighting is necessary.
Return along the same opened pedestrian deck. Yield to walkers and bikes and do not stop where a narrow approach or crossing needs room.
Write an outward observation, a return observation and your actual turnaround. Add one detail that looked different with direction; the planning minutes are not a pace target.
